summary:
[  edit  ]
The Text  SOP  creates text geometry from any  TrueType  or  OpenType  font that is installed on the system, or any TrueType/OpenType font file on disk.  Unicode  is supported.
See also:  Text TOP ,  Unicode .

parameters.label: Font
parameters.name: font
parameters.description: Select the font for the text from this drop down menu. All fonts are provided by the OS, any  TrueType  font that is loaded into the OS can be used.

parameters.label: Font File
parameters.name: fontfile
parameters.description: Specify any TrueType or OpenType font file ( .ttf, .otf file ) to use for the text. When using a font file, the Font menu above is disabled.

parameters.label: Bold
parameters.name: bold
parameters.description: Displays the text in  bold .

parameters.label: Italic
parameters.name: italic
parameters.description: Displays the text in  Italic .

parameters.label: Font Size X
parameters.name: fontsizex
parameters.description: Sets the font size in X (horizontal). The font size defines the distance from the baseline to the top of the layout box for the given font. The default size of 1 of the default font is close to the vertical size of capital letters with no descenders.

parameters.label: Font Size Y
parameters.name: fontsizey
parameters.description: Sets the font size in Y (vertical).

parameters.label: Keep Font Ratio
parameters.name: keepfontratio
parameters.description: Ignores Y value in Font Size. Sets both X and Y size to  Font Size  X.

parameters.label: Scale Font to BBox Height
parameters.name: scalefontobboxheight
parameters.description: Scale the font’s vertical size so it’s based on the vertical bounding box of the font.

parameters.label: Output
parameters.name: output
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify geometry output of Triangles, Closed Polygons or Open Polygons.

parameters.label: Triangles
parameters.name: triangles
parameters.description: The output is a triangulated mesh suitable for shaded renders.

parameters.label: Closed Polygons (Filled Holes)
parameters.name: closedpolys
parameters.description: The output is a set of separated closed outlines, suitable for  Laser CHOP ,  Extrude SOP , etc.  Append a  Hole SOP  to preserve holes properly.

parameters.label: Open Polygons
parameters.name: openpolys
parameters.description: The output is a set of separated open outlines, suitable for the  Laser CHOP , etc. Renders as a wireframe always.

parameters.label: Level of Detail
parameters.name: levelofdetail
parameters.description: Controls the quality of the text's shape by adding/removing subdivisions to the geometry.

parameters.label: Language
parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language type hint to help format the glyphs correctly. This should be a abbreviation from the  Text TOP/SOP Unicode Language Abbreviations  table.

parameters.label: Reading Direction
parameters.name: readingdirection
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use to set whether the language reads Left to Right or Right to Left.

parameters.label: Kerning
parameters.name: kerning
parameters.description: ⊞  - The amount of space to add between letters in X and Y. Kerning is way of adding an arbitrary offset between letters. There already is a default offset associated with each font so the letters are flush against each other. The  Kerning  parameter this adds to that and allows for a Y offset.

parameters.label: Line Spacing
parameters.name: linespacing
parameters.description: Determines the amount of space between lines of text.

parameters.label: Horizontal Align
parameters.name: alignx
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the horizontal alignment.

parameters.label: Left
parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Left justifies the text.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centers the text.

parameters.label: Right
parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Right justifies the text.

parameters.label: Word Wrap
parameters.name: wordwrap
parameters.description: When checked text is automatically line wrapped once it takes up the space set in  Word Wrap Size  parameter below.

parameters.label: Word Wrap Size
parameters.name: wordwrapsize
parameters.description: Determines the amount of 3D space used before the line wraps.

parameters.label: Text
parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The string of text to create as geometry.  If newlines or tabs are desired, the recommended way is to change this parameter to expression mode, and specify a Python string that includes \n or \t to signify newlines and tabs. E.g  'First Line\nSecond Line' .

parameters.label: Legacy Parsing
parameters.name: legacyparsing
parameters.description: Note, it's recommended to use a Python expression in the Text parameter instead of enabling legacy parsing, as this parsing can easily run into issues with more complex strings.  When enabled and if the Text parameter is in Constant Mode, \t and \n character sequences will be turned into tab and newline characters respectively. Otherwise the \t and \n sequences will be left as literal \ and t and \ and n.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the overall transform order for the transformations. The transform order determines the order in which transformations take place. Depending on the order, you can achieve different results using the exact same values. Choose the appropriate order from the menu.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the order of the rotations within the overall transform order.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields move the geometry in the three axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields rotate the geometry in the three axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields scale the geometry in the three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - The pivot point for the transformations (not the same as the pivot point in the pivot channels). The pivot point parameters allow you to define the point about which geometry scales and rotates. Altering the pivot point produces different results depending on the transformation performed on the object.

parameters.label: For example, during a scaling operation, if the pivot point of an object is located at:
parameters.description: 1, -1, 0  and you wanted to scale the object by  0.5  (reduce its size by 50%) the object would scale toward the pivot point and appear to slide down and to the left.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

Las primitivas de punto, por ejemplo, son primitivas de un solo vértice renderizadas como puntos, ideales para nubes de puntos o sistemas de partículas.7 Una distinción clave con respecto a los SOPs es que los POPs actualmente no admiten primitivas de curva directamente, aunque la subdivisión de splines es posible utilizando operadores como Line POP y Line Divide POP.7 Los atributos son cruciales para almacenar datos adicionales por punto, vértice o primitiva, como normales (N), coordenadas de textura (uv) y color (Cd).1 Los POPs permiten la creación, modificación, duplicación, cambio de nombre y eliminación de estos atributos.1 El énfasis en los "atributos" y su manipulación a través de varios POPs (por ejemplo, Attribute POP, GLSL POP, Math Mix POP) apunta a una filosofía de diseño centrada en los atributos para los POPs. Te permite **crear nuevos atributos**, **renombrar atributos existentes**, **duplicarlos** o **eliminarlos**. * **Características clave:** * **Crear nuevos atributos**: Cuando creas uno, puedes especificar: * Su **nombre** (puedes usar nombres predefinidos como `P` para posición, `N` para normales, `Color` para color, `Tex` para coordenadas de textura, o crear el tuyo propio). * Su **tipo de dato** (`float`, `double`, `int`, `uint`). * El **número de componentes** (1, 2, 3 o 4).
